This integration connects Gladys to your **Beatbot pool robots** (AquaSense,
Sora… ranges) and their **cleaning base station**, through the Beatbot cloud.

## Before you start

- Your robots must already work in the **Beatbot app** (account created, robot
  paired, Wi-Fi set up).
- Beatbot robots are controlled **through the Beatbot cloud only**: Gladys
  needs Internet access. There is no local control.
- A diving robot often loses Wi-Fi: it then shows as **unreachable** for a few
  minutes, which is expected.

## Linking the account

1. Open the **Configuration** tab of the integration.
2. Click **Connect** next to **Beatbot account**.
3. The Beatbot sign-in page opens: sign in and allow access. Your password is
   typed on Beatbot's page, it never goes through Gladys.
4. Back in Gladys, the connection status turns green and your robots show up
   in the **Discover** tab: click **Add to Gladys** on each one.

The **Test the connection** button lists the robots found, their status and
their battery.

### The other settings

| Setting             | What it is for                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Region**          | Where your account is hosted (Europe, North America, China). **Automatic** reads it from the account: change it only when asked. |
| **Full refresh**    | States arrive in real time. This full read (every 10 min by default) catches what a network outage made you miss.                |
| **OAuth client ID** | Advanced. Keep the default unless Beatbot gave you another client ID.                                                            |

### If Connect does nothing

Gladys opens the Beatbot sign-in page in a new tab. If no tab opens, the
browser most likely blocked it as a pop-up (Safari on iPhone and iPad does it
often): allow pop-ups for the address of your Gladys (on iPhone: **Settings →
Apps → Safari → Block Pop-ups**, off), or use a computer, then click
**Connect** again.

The `home-assistant` value of **OAuth client ID** is only the name of the
public client Beatbot publishes for home automation: you do not need Home
Assistant.

### If the Beatbot page refuses the sign-in

The integration uses the "open API" access Beatbot publishes for home
automation, with Beatbot's public client ID.

**Known issue: "Whitelabel Error Page … status=400".** After you type your
email and password, the Beatbot page may show:

```
Whitelabel Error Page
There was an unexpected error (type=Bad Request, status=400).
```

- This is not your password: the Beatbot page checks the return address of
  Gladys only after the sign-in, and does not accept it yet for the public
  client ID.
- A request is open at Beatbot to accept Gladys: follow it on
  [GitHub](https://github.com/Beatbot-Robotics/beatbot-cloud-python/issues/6). Nothing can be fixed on the Gladys side until then.
- You are now signed in at Beatbot, so every new try goes straight to this
  error. To start again from the sign-in page, use a private browser window
  (or delete the cookies of `oauth.beatbot.com`).
- If Beatbot gives you a client ID for Gladys, type it in **OAuth client ID**,
  save, then click **Connect** again.

## What you get

For every robot (and every station), depending on what the robot offers:

| Feature                    | Detail                                                                            |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **State**                  | Stopped, cleaning, paused, error, returning, charging, docked.                    |
| **Cleaning**               | Start / pause the cleaning.                                                       |
| **Return to base**         | Calls the robot back (to its base, or to the waterline for pickup).               |
| **Battery** / **Charging** | Battery level in % and charging in progress (robots only, not the station).       |
| **Cleaning mode**          | The robot's modes (floor, walls, waterline…), named as Beatbot names them.        |
| **Child lock**             | Locks the robot's buttons.                                                        |
| **Do not disturb**         | Turns the robot's voice prompts off (read-only when the robot does not allow it). |

Every robot carries a **cloud** badge when reachable, **unreachable** otherwise.

## Scenes

The integration adds its own cards to the scene editor (Gladys 5.1 or later),
under **Integrations**.

Triggers:

- **Pool robot status changed** — optionally filter on the robot and on the
  new status. The next actions read `{{triggerEvent.data.status}}`,
  `{{triggerEvent.data.previous_status}}` and `{{triggerEvent.data.detail}}`
  (detailed status: diving, surfacing…).
- **Pool cleaning finished** — a cycle ended normally. Variables:
  `{{triggerEvent.data.duration_minutes}}` (empty when the cycle started before
  the integration did) and `{{triggerEvent.data.battery}}`.
- **Pool robot fault** — a fault just appeared (robot stuck, basket full, motor
  fault…). Filter on the faults you care about. Variables:
  `{{triggerEvent.data.error}}`, `{{triggerEvent.data.label_en}}`.

Actions (each one returns `sent`: false when the robot does not offer that
order):

- **Start pool cleaning**
- **Pause pool cleaning**
- **Send the pool robot back**
- **Set the cleaning mode** — type the mode name as shown on the device in
  Gladys.

Examples: "when the cleaning is finished, send me a message with its
duration", or "when the robot is stuck, alert me".

## Dashboard

In **Dashboard → Edit → New widget**, add the **Pool robot** widget (under
**Integration widgets**) and pick the robot: it shows the live battery,
the status, the current fault, the link, the mode and how long the last
cleaning took, with **Start**, **Pause** and **Return** buttons.

When the robot lets its cleaning mode be changed, a **Cleaning mode** button
opens a small form listing the modes of that robot, pre-filled with the current
one: pick one and send it (Gladys 5.2 or later, required by the integration).

## Troubleshooting

- **"Click Connect…"**: no account linked, or the authorization expired or was
  revoked: click **Connect** again.
- **"Your Beatbot account did not give its region"**: choose it in **Region**
  and save.
- **"Beatbot cloud unreachable"**: check Gladys' Internet access; the
  integration retries on its own.
- **States no longer move in real time**: another software (Home Assistant for
  instance) may use the same Beatbot account and have taken the real-time
  connection. States are still updated at every full refresh.
- The integration logs are in its **Logs** tab in Gladys. They never contain your
  tokens.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Beatbot asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | Your robots must already work in the Beatbot app. Click Connect and sign in with your Beatbot account: Gladys then finds every pool robot of the account. Beatbot robots are reached through the Beatbot cloud only, Internet access is required. |
| Beatbot account | `oauth2` | No | Opens the Beatbot sign-in page. Your password never goes through Gladys. |
| Region | `select` | No | Where your Beatbot account is hosted. Automatic reads it from the account: change it only if the connection status asks you to. |
| Full refresh (minutes) | `number` | No | States arrive in real time; this periodic full read only catches what a network outage made you miss. |
| OAuth client ID (advanced) | `string` | No | Leave as is unless Beatbot gave you another client ID. "home-assistant" is only the name of the public client Beatbot publishes: you do not need Home Assistant. Click Connect again after changing it. |

## How to install Beatbot in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Beatbot appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/prohand/gladys-beatbot:1.2.3`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/prohand/gladys-beatbot](https://github.com/prohand/gladys-beatbot).

Beatbot requires Gladys `>=5.2.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Beatbot is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [prohand](https://github.com/prohand), not by the Gladys core team.
